questions.q: What is this lesson's own explicit framing of its content?
options: Orientation, not legal advice — any real compliance decision needs a qualified professional and the current primary text
A complete, authoritative legal compliance checklist
A guarantee that following it makes an organization compliant
A substitute for consulting a lawyer in any jurisdiction
questions.explain: The lesson repeats, deliberately, that it is orientation only and not a basis for a real compliance decision.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what is the key difference between a framework and a regulation?
options: A framework is something an organization chooses to follow; a regulation is required by a government body with real enforcement
A framework always costs more money to implement than a regulation
There is no meaningful difference between the two
A regulation is always older than any framework
questions.explain: The lesson's core distinction is voluntary adoption (framework) versus government-required compliance with enforcement (regulation).

questions.q: Why does the lesson say 'no AI law yet' was never the same as 'no legal exposure'?
options: Because existing data-protection and employment law already apply to a lot of AI activity, even without AI-specific rules
Because every country already has a comprehensive AI law
Because AI systems are not subject to any law anywhere
Because only sector regulators can ever have jurisdiction over AI
questions.explain: The lesson explains that existing law already covers much AI activity, so a lack of AI-specific law didn't mean zero exposure.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the recurring regulatory patterns the lesson names?
options: Transparency obligations requiring people be told when they're interacting with or evaluated by an AI system
A requirement that all AI models be open source
A ban on AI systems with more than one data source
A requirement that every model be retrained every 24 hours
questions.explain: Transparency obligations are one of the four recurring patterns the lesson names, along with risk tiering, documentation, and human oversight.

questions.q: What does the lesson recommend as the practical next step for an organization's actual regulatory obligations?
options: Recognize the recurring patterns, then build a program structure that can absorb whatever a qualified legal review determines applies
Assume the EU AI Act applies identically to every organization worldwide
Ignore regulation entirely until a lawsuit is filed
Treat this single lesson as the final word on compliance
questions.explain: The lesson points to pattern-recognition plus a real legal review and a program structure (Lesson 30) as the practical path forward.
